title.narrative: Lao PDR Financial Sector Safety Net Strengthening

description.narrative: The development objective of the Financial Sector Safety Net Strengthening Project for Lao People's Democratic Republic is to strengthen the financial and institutional capacity of the deposit protection office (DPO) to fulfill its deposit insurance mandate. The project comprises of two components. The first component, capitalization of DPO equity fund will use performance-based conditions (PBCs), whereby the World Bank funds are disbursed in tranches based upon verification of achievement of the pre-agreed PBCs. The second component, institutional capacity building for DPO and project management will finance select technical assistance (TA) to strengthen the DPO's institutional capacity and to complement parallel and ongoing TA financed by the World Bank. This component will also finance consultants to support project implementation, including the following functions: project coordinator, communications, financial management (FM), and procurement.
To strengthen the financial and institutional capacity of the Deposit Protection Office to fulfill its deposit insurance mandate.

condition.narrative: Environmental and Social StandardsFinancing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.FRecurrent, Continuous The Recipient shall causethe Project Implementing Entity to ensure that the Project is carried out in accordance with the Environmental and SocialStandards, in a manner acceptable to the Association.

Financing under Part 1 of the Project based on PBCsFinancing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.GRecurrent, Continuous 1. TheRecipient shall cause the Project Implementing Entity to:(a) implement Part 1 of the Project in accordance with the institutional,environmental and social risk management, financial management and procurement arrangements set out in this Schedule 2 to thisAgreement;(b) throughout the period of implementation of said part of the Project as necessary, carry out verification todetermine whether the PBCs have been met as detailed in the POM; and (c) furnish said assessment to the Association for itsreview. 2. (a) The amount of payments which the Recipient may request for PBC- based financing under Part 1 of the Project shallbe determined on the basis of the maximum amount allocated by the Association to each PBC, subject to the provisions of Section IIIof this Schedule 2, provided that such amount shall not exceed the total amount of payment for Eligible Expenditures incurredduring the year covered by the PBC-based financing payment requested, excluding any amount of eligible expenditures financed fromother sources of financing.(b) Notwithstanding the provision of sub-paragraph (a) of this sub-section 2, all payments under thePBC-based financing shall be subject to the Association's prior written approval and shall only be eligible for financing out ofthe proceeds of the Financing if and to the extent approved by the Association in accordance with the provisions of Section III ofthis Schedule.

PBC Monitoring and ReportingFinancing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.ERecurrent, ContinuousWithout limitation on its otherreporting obligations under this Agreement, the Recipient shall cause the Project Implementing Entity, not later than November 30of each year during the Project implementation period, to furnish reports to the Association on the status of achievement of therelevant PBC Targets, in accordance with the Verification Protocols and procedures set out in the Project Operational Manual.

Project Operations ManualFinancing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.CRecurrent, Continuous1. The Recipient shall cause theProject Implementing Entity to ensure that the Project is carried out in accordance with the arrangements and procedures set out inthe Project Operations Manual satisfactory to the Association, that includes, inter alia, detailed arrangements and procedures for:(i) institutional coordination and day-to-day execution of the Project; (ii) disbursement, financial management and procurement;(iii) environmental and social safeguards management; (iv) a verification protocol containing the technical standards andarrangements and procedures for the monitoring, reporting and verification of PBCs; (v) monitoring, evaluation, reporting andcommunication; and (vi) such other administrative, financial, technical and organizational arrangements and procedures as shall berequired for the Project.
Restructuring would extend the deadline for compliance with legal covenant from 18 months after effectiveness to 21 months aftereffectiveness.

Subsidiary AgreementFinancing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.BRecurrent, Continuous1. To facilitate the carrying out ofthe Project, the Recipient shall make the proceeds of the Financing available to the Project Implementing Entity under a subsidiaryagreement between the Recipient and the Project Implementing Entity, under terms and conditions acceptable to the Association (theSubsidiary Agreement). 2. The Recipient shall exercise its rights under the Subsidiary Agreement in such manner as to protectthe interests of the Recipient, and the Association and to accomplish the purposes of the Financing. Except as the Associationshall otherwise agree, the Recipient shall not assign, amend, abrogate or waive the Subsidiary Agreement or any of its provisions.

title.narrative: Timely payout of insured deposits in the event of a bank failure, pursuant to Decree on Deposit Protection

comment.narrative: In the event that there is no bank failure, the preparedness of DPO to undertake a deposit insurance claims processing and payout in a timely manner, shall be assessed based on the results of a simulation exercise to be conducted in 2025. During the 7-day simulation period, DPO should complete the following prerequisites to undertake a payout process (a) Payout Plan; (b) Payout Team to be deployed; (c) Data processing and validation; (d) Financing, Logistics and other requirements and sourcing; and (e) Depositor assistance strategy. WB shall assess the acceptability of these plans and DPO's ability to implement the plans during the 7-day simulation period.

title.narrative: Percentage of complaints handled from Grievance Redress mechanism in place (disaggregated by number/percent of women)

comment.narrative:
No complaints or grievance messages were received by DPO to date. The grievance mechanism has been set up. DPO has assigned focal person, who will coordinate with an Internal Audit Division staff to manage and maintain the GRM for PIU. The DPO has also set up a hotline, comments/feedback section on their official website, social media pitch and office drop box for comments, complaints, and feedbacks. Training for PIU, DPO staff, and members on managing clients feedback and complaints was conducted in early March 2023 after the Communication Consultant came on board.
Draft Public awareness strategy contains plans for grievance mechanism, including via website and other facilities for grievance and complaints by depositors. Indicator will track percentage of registered grievances that are addressed according to agreed procedures. This is the total number of grievance messages received by [website and other facilities], which have been satisfactorily addressed and recorded.

title.narrative: DPO empowered to perform its legally-mandated function (deposit payout), as evidenced by progress towards compliance with IADI Core Principles

comment.narrative:
DPO and WB updated the self-assessment of DPO performance against the IADI Core Principles in March 2023. DPO has made improvement, scoring 63% compared to 50% in 2019, still considered Materially non-compliant (MNC). The final assessment under the project is on-going. To achieve the target, DPO must complete outstanding PBCs and integrate completed ones into operations. Issues and requirements for the assessment were identified. Upon completion of the assessment expected in February 2026, this indicator will be updated.
The scoring system is based on 16 core principles (each with sub-criteria), with percentages assigned as: NA=0% (not applicable), NC=Non-compliant (25%), MNC=50% (materially non-compliant), LC=75% (largely compliant), C=100% (compliant). The baseline is 57% (materially non-compliant). The target assumes DPO achieves all PBCs, corresponding to a 74% rating (partially compliant). The World Bank will periodically update the assessment during project implementation.

title.narrative: Adequate financial inflows into the deposit insurance fund during the course of the project, in order to achieve a funding ratio of at least 0.52% (eligible deposits)

comment.narrative:
DPO reported that the project's current TFR is at 0.64%, which exceeds the target of 0.52%. The figure will be reviewed for consistency with the strategy that will be finalized taking into account risks on the banking system and impact of non-bank financial institutions to arrive at the TFR. The strategy is expected to be completed in February, at which time the figure will be updated.
This revision from 1.1% to 0.52% target was due to the prevailing economic conditions that significantly impact and influence key variables to project the target fund ratio, including the growth and behavior of deposits, the foreign currency composition of insured deposits, sources of funds that contribute to deposit protection reserve fund, and operating expenses. These estimates do not assume payout of liabilities to depositors arising from the closure of member institutions and shall require an adjustment to the premium rate charged to member institutions
